prompt:
THE ENTIRE BACKGROUND MUST BE SOLID PURE MAGENTA, RGB(255,0,255), edge to edge, filling every pixel that is not the cross itself — a flat chroma-key backdrop, NOT white, NOT grey, NOT a coloured wash, NOT a gradient, NOT a vignette, NOT a scene, NOT a sky, NOT a hill, NOT a border or frame. No ground, no cast shadow, no horizon, no rope, no nails, no text, no watermark, no second copy, no silhouette. All four corners of the image must be that same flat magenta.

EXACTLY ONE OBJECT AND NO PEOPLE. This is the cross ALONE — no figure carrying it, no hands, no arms, no shoulder, no crowd, no second cross beside it. Just the timber.

PROPORTIONS ARE THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THIS IMAGE. This is a TALL, LONG-BEAMED CARRYING CROSS, not a small stubby wall crucifix. THE WHOLE CROSS MUST BE ABOUT TWICE AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE — the image is portrait, clearly taller than it is wide. The long vertical beam is the dominant shape and runs the FULL height of the image. The short horizontal crossbeam sits HIGH, about one quarter of the way down from the top, and the length of the beam BELOW the crossbeam is roughly THREE TIMES the length of the stub above it — a long trailing beam that would drag on the ground. The crossbeam's total span is only about HALF the height of the whole cross, so it is clearly the shorter of the two timbers. Do not make the crossbeam as wide as the cross is tall.

STANDING PERFECTLY UPRIGHT AND SQUARE TO THE VIEWER, NOT tilted, NOT leaning, NOT angled, NOT in perspective, NOT lying down and NOT seen from below. The long beam runs straight up and down, exactly vertical, dead centre. The crossbeam is exactly horizontal. The WHOLE cross is inside the frame — the top of the beam, both ends of the crossbeam, and the FOOT of the long beam — with a little magenta visible all the way around it, including below the foot. Do not crop the bottom of the beam.

A rough-hewn carpenter's cross of two heavy weathered timbers, bark stripped, the saw and adze marks still showing, the grain running along each beam, the corners knocked and worn. Warm mid-brown wood with darker grain and a few deeper knots. The beams simply cross, with no lashing and no joinery detail. Warm hand-illustrated storybook style, clean shapes and soft painted shading, no line art, no photorealism, no cel-shading outlines. Lit warmly from the upper left so the left face of each beam is lighter and the right face falls into a soft brown shadow. Colours and values separated clearly enough that the shape still reads as a cross when the whole object is only 60 pixels tall against a dark background.
